title: Enumeration of Billions of Maximal Bicliques in Bipartite Graphs without Using GPUs
problem: Maximal biclique enumeration (MBE) on bipartite graphs suffers from redundant memory accesses and degraded set intersection performance because computational subgraphs dynamically change during enumeration. Existing algorithms cannot scale to enumerate billions of bicliques on large real-world datasets.
motivation: Maximal biclique enumeration is crucial for bipartite graph analysis with applications to large-scale graph datasets.
method: AdaMBE redesigns core operations using local neighborhood information from computational subgraphs to minimize redundant memory accesses. It dynamically constructs computational subgraphs using bitmaps with fast bitwise operations to accelerate set intersections. A parallel version (ParAdaMBE) distributes the computation across multiple CPU cores.
key_novelty: Using dynamic bitmap-based computational subgraphs to reduce redundant memory accesses and accelerate set intersections in biclique enumeration.
contributions: AdaMBE algorithm with optimized core operations leveraging local neighborhood information from computational subgraphs
Bitmap-based dynamic computational subgraph construction with fast bitwise operations for set intersection acceleration
Successfully enumerates 19 billion maximal bicliques on TVTropes dataset, enabling unprecedented scale
Parallel CPU version (ParAdaMBE) achieves 5.07× speedup over GPU-based GMBE system

metrics.speedup: 1.6×-49.7× vs closest CPU competitor; 5.07× vs GPU-based GMBE
metrics.other: 19 billion maximal bicliques on TVTropes dataset

primary_theme: CPU-optimized maximal biclique enumeration using bitmap-accelerated set intersections
